messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout completed: release v2.14.0 -> runtime-cluster-eu-west-1. Monitoring: latency SLO breach detected (p50 and p95 up) for /v1/generate; triggered at 1763334800.

pagerduty-bot: Paging maya (oncall) — Priority P1 — metric: runtime.request_latency.p95 > 450ms (5m) — escalations enabled.

maya (oncall): saw the page, looking. Any known deploys?

liam (eng-runtime): I pushed the canary earlier, yes v2.14.0 had token-parallel batching changes + fallback kernel tweak. Canary was small (10% traffic) but I'm seeing latency jump on canary hosts in the metrics.

sam (eng-sre): Confirming. infra graphs show canary nodes have high syscalls/wakeup spikes and CPU waiting on GPU memcpy. Throughput also degraded ~30% on those nodes.

maya (oncall): copying logs from canary node rtf-13:
```
[runtime] 2026-03-? 12:33:42 WARN kernel_fallback: kernel select failed for attention_v2 -> falling back to slower kernel
[runtime] 2026-03-? 12:33:42 INFO batching: batch_size_target=32 but processing latency increased -> dynamic_batching reduced
[rtf-13] oom_killer: no
```

liam (eng-runtime): That kernel_fallback line is the smoking gun. The new kernel selection logic is preferring a kernel variant that triggers a fallback path on our older driver stack. We didn't catch the fallback perf delta in canary smoke because sequence length distribution was biased.

olivia (prodops): Customer impact? Any 5xx spikes? Aaron anything from CS?

aaron (customer-suc): We have three customers reporting elevated latencies in EU and one internal alert about timeouts on long-context jobs. No wide 5xx yet, mostly timeouts > 10s on heavy prompts.

sam (eng-sre): 5xxs stay low — just timeouts and queuing. If it continues for next 15m we should escalate to SEV.

maya (oncall): Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) Kill the canary rollout (stop traffic to canary hosts) 2) Roll back canary service to v2.13.9 or 3) Flip feature-flag to force previous kernel selection. Which is fastest?

liam (eng-runtime): Quickest is to drain canary nodes (stop routing) — that will remove the bad kernel from serving path without touching feature flags. I can push a rollback but that takes ~5–7 min with canary. Feature flag flip requires a config push to config service which is fast but we need to be 100% sure there are no side effects.

sam (eng-sre): I can disable the canary in the load-balancer now. Doing: `kubectl patch svc runtime-cluster-eu-west --patch '{"spec": {"canaryPercent": 0}}'`

sam (eng-sre): done — removed canary routing. Health checks are green, average latency back to baseline on global graphs within 2m.

maya (oncall): Confirming metrics — p95 fell from ~520ms to ~120ms on the service. Great.

liam (eng-runtime): Thanks Sam. I'll open a rollback PR for v2.14.0 -> revert token-parallel batching changes and adjust kernel selector to guard on driver capabilities.

olivia (prodops): Communication: I'll draft a short blurb for status page: "Investigating elevated latency after a small canary rollout; traffic diverted and rollbacks in progress; limited customer impact." Aaron, can you surface to impacted customers?

aaron (customer-suc): Yep — emailed the three customers with ETA and mitigation note. One replied asking for root cause once available.

maya (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm pausing alerts for 20m while rollback/verification proceeds. If latency regression reappears, page immediately and escalate to SEV chat. Next on-call (liam) will own further follow-ups after 14:00 UTC.

liam (eng-runtime): I'll monitor. Quick sanity checks to run for post-rollback: 1) confirm kernel_fallback log absent on new hosts 2) run seqlen=2048 benchmark against canary replay traffic 3) check batching behavior with load tests. I'll post results here.

sam (eng-sre): After rollback, host rtf-13 logs no longer show kernel_fallback lines. Batching stabilized.

liam (eng-runtime): Benchmarks: ran replay with heavy prompts -> throughput back to expected and p95 matches baseline. Kernel selector now instrumented to emit capability flags; will submit a guarded patch and tests tomorrow.

olivia (prodops): Status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Resolved — traffic diverted from canary. We are rolling back the canary release and monitoring. No broad customer outage"

aaron (customer-suc): Customers acknowledged — two said deal ok, one asked for a postmortem.

maya (oncall): Creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem. Tags: release-regression, kernel-fallback, canary.

liam (eng-runtime): Will take PM for postmortem. Drafting timeline and will include actionable: add smoke test with long-sequence distribution, add a fallback perf regression alert, and a feature-flag to force kernel path for emergency.

maya (oncall): Handing off: liam you're oncall for incident follow-ups after 14:00 UTC. I'll mark this thread as monitored and close after verification window.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved at 1763336985.

maya (oncall): Closing notes — root cause: kernel selection change in v2.14.0 led to runtime falling back to slower kernel on certain driver stacks under long-sequence workloads; canary detected due to 10% traffic sampling; immediate mitigation was remove canary routing; rollback + instrumentation in progress. Postmortem to include timeline and test coverage.

liam (eng-runtime): Thanks all. I'll ping when postmortem draft is ready.

olivia (prodops): Nice quick mitigation. Please include a runbook step for kill-switch path (feature-flag + LB drain) in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

maya (oncall): Logged incident ticket ID INC-2026-0315-47 and linked related PRs to it.

sam (eng-sre): Adding runbook note: when kernel_fallback spikes and p95>300ms, first action: drain canary, then / then rollback.

liam (eng-runtime): Putting a checklist in the PR description for rollout criteria and a QA job that runs seqlen=2048 tests on candidate images.

maya (oncall): End of thread — monitoring window complete, closing at 1763337000.
